program_basics-01.why: Most students know print, but multiple arguments add spaces by default, which can trick some.

program_basics-02.why: Using the end parameter is a new concept and easily misread by beginners.

program_basics-03.why: The print function is introduced on day one and reinforced constantly.

comments-01.why: The hash symbol for comments is a standard Python basic, though some might confuse it with other languages.

comments-02.why: Straightforward execution trace, but inline comments can occasionally confuse absolute beginners.

comments-03.why: Conceptual explanation is usually well understood after the first lecture.

variables-01.why: Re-assignment is a core concept taught early; students quickly learn state updates.

variables-02.why: Variables hold values, not references to other variables in a reactive way; this is a classic beginner pitfall.

variables-03.why: Naming rules (no dashes, no spaces, cannot start with a number) are straightforward.

strings-01.why: Students often expect arithmetic addition rather than string concatenation since the characters look like numbers.

strings-02.why: String multiplication is intuitive and usually demonstrated clearly.

strings-03.why: Quotes inside strings require escaping or alternating quotes, a common initial stumbling block.

strings-04.why: Writing a simple function using f-strings or concatenation is standard practice.

function_calls-01.why: Keyword arguments are introduced alongside print; naming them can be tricky at first.

function_calls-02.why: Printing the return value of print() yields None, which is surprising to beginners.

function_calls-03.why: Terminology like 'argument' is emphasized early on.

user_input-01.why: Beginners frequently forget that input() returns a string, even when numbers are typed.

user_input-02.why: Directly follows from the previous point; string concatenation causes 5 + 1 to become '51'.

user_input-03.why: Explaining type casting (int()) is a staple exercise in CS50P.

string_methods-01.why: strip() is straightforward and visually verifiable.

string_methods-02.why: title() capitalizes every word, which is intuitive.

string_methods-03.why: Chaining string methods (strip().title()) is a slightly advanced beginner task.

string_methods-04.why: Multiple assignment with split() can be confusing for students who haven't seen list unpacking.

f_strings-01.why: f-strings are heavily promoted as the best way to format strings in modern Python.

f_strings-02.why: Float formatting syntax (:.2f) involves specific syntax that students must memorize.

f_strings-03.why: Comma separator syntax in f-strings is a very specific formatting trick that beginners easily forget.

f_strings-04.why: Requires combining f-string formatting specifiers with function definition, which tests syntax memory.

integers-01.why: Floor division is taught explicitly, though some confuse it with standard division returning a float.

integers-02.why: Distinguishing integer literals from floats and strings is fundamental and well-grasped.

integers-03.why: Many beginners expect 10 / 2 to return an int (5), forgetting that division always produces a float.

arithmetic_operators-01.why: Standard order of operations applies, though a few might compute left-to-right yielding 20.

arithmetic_operators-02.why: Exponentiation operator is intuitive, though occasionally confused with multiplication.

arithmetic_operators-03.why: Basic math function with parameters and return value is straightforward for beginners.

arithmetic_operators-04.why: Compound assignment operators require tracking state step-by-step; easy to make minor arithmetic slips.

floats-01.why: Rounding to 2 decimal places is intuitive and matches standard expectations.

floats-02.why: Floating-point precision issues surprise almost all beginners when first encountered.

floats-03.why: Explaining IEEE 754 precision and math.isclose() is conceptually advanced for day one.

floats-04.why: Translating a formula into code and applying round() is a standard practice task.

type_conversion-01.why: Explicit type casting prevents string concatenation, yielding the obvious numeric sum.

type_conversion-02.why: Beginners often mistakenly think int() rounds to the nearest integer instead of truncating.

type_conversion-03.why: Many expect int('3.5') to return 3, not realizing it triggers a ValueError.

type_conversion-04.why: Combining input/string conversion into an addition task is a classic beginner exercise.

indentation_blocks-01.why: Tracing conditional blocks is straightforward once indentation rules are understood.

indentation_blocks-02.why: Missing indentation after a colon is the most common syntax error for beginners.

indentation_blocks-03.why: Whitespace significance is heavily emphasized in Python courses.

defining_functions-01.why: Students learn quickly that defining a function does not execute its body automatically.

defining_functions-02.why: NameError occurs because functions must be defined before they are called in Python.

defining_functions-03.why: Writing a simple single-parameter function is universally practiced.

defining_functions-04.why: Reusability and maintainability are core concepts taught immediately with functions.

parameters-01.why: Default arguments are clear, though tracing multiple calls requires careful reading.

modulo-03.why: Python's modulo with negative numbers confuses beginners.

match_statement-01.why: Straightforward match syntax introduced in CS50P.

match_statement-02.why: Wildcard pattern _ is standard default case.

match_statement-03.why: Writing a match function requires remembering syntax.

while_loops-03.why: Arithmetic loop for digits is tricky for beginners.

while_loops-04.why: Collatz requires careful loop condition and logic.

range_function-01.why: Step argument in range often confuses start/stop boundaries.

range_function-03.why: len of range involves subtracting endpoints.

for_loops-01.why: Accumulator pattern with for loop is standard.

for_loops-02.why: String multiplication inside loop is intuitive.

for_loops-03.why: Variable reassignment instead of accumulation trips up many.

break_continue-01.why: Break statement behavior is easy to grasp.

break_continue-02.why: Continue skips the print for even numbers, tricky to trace.

break_continue-03.why: Early return or break pattern for searching lists.

lists-01.why: Zero-based indexing is taught early and often.

lists-02.why: IndexError is the standard out-of-bounds error.

lists-04.why: Negative indexing or empty check is required.

iterating_lists-02.why: Rebinding loop variable n does not mutate the list.

iterating_lists-03.why: Finding maximum requires tracking current max.

nested_loops-01.why: Tracing grid prints with end='' requires careful tracking.

nested_loops-02.why: Requires list comprehensions or nested loops with row construction, tricky for beginners.

nested_loops-03.why: Tracing dependent ranges (range(i)) often trips students up (outputs 0+1+2 = 3).

dictionaries-01.why: Direct dictionary key lookup is a straightforward and well-understood concept.

dictionaries-02.why: Accessing a missing key correctly raises a KeyError, which is introduced right away.

dictionaries-03.why: Building frequency maps with the .get() method or 'in' check requires practice.

dictionaries-04.why: Students learn that keys are unique and assignment overwrites existing values.

nested_data-01.why: Combining list indexing and dictionary key lookup is standard after one lesson.

nested_data-02.why: Iterating over a list of dicts and conditionally building a result list takes a few steps.

nested_data-03.why: Negative indexing combined with nested dictionary access can confuse some.

try_except-01.why: Control flow in try-except is clear: exception caught, rest of try skipped, outside code runs.

try_except-02.why: Simple return value on failure pattern is common, but syntax needs precision.

try_except-03.why: The else block in try/except is easily forgotten by beginners.

try_except-04.why: The danger of bare excepts is heavily emphasized in Python courses.

try_except-05.why: ZeroDivisionError is specific and easy to remember after seeing it once.

try_except-06.why: Explaining the infinite loop and break on success is a classic pattern.

imports-01.why: Common mistake forgetting math.sqrt() vs sqrt() directly.

imports-02.why: Direct function import syntax from module is practiced frequently.

imports-03.why: Pseudo-random seed determinism is usually understood when demonstrated.

slicing-01.why: Stop index exclusivity (s[1:4]) is a classic beginner hurdle.

slicing-02.why: Negative step size for reversing strings is a fun trick quickly learned.

slicing-03.why: Using slice notation [1:-1] for removing ends is a clean, standard idiom.

slicing-04.why: Negative slicing from the end [-2:] is well-grasped after examples.

command_line_args-01.why: Remembering that sys.argv includes the script name itself is a common slip-up.

command_line_args-02.why: Conditional checks on list length before indexing argv is standard boilerplate.

command_line_args-03.why: IndexError prevention is the primary reason taught for checking len(sys.argv).

packages_pip-01.why: Direct recall of the basic pip command.

packages_pip-02.why: Common rookie error, but straightforward troubleshooting.

packages_pip-03.why: Requires explaining both PyPI and pip in writing.

apis_json-01.why: json.loads parses JSON dict into Python dict; age is int 36.

apis_json-02.why: Core concept of web APIs returning JSON data.

apis_json-03.why: List comprehension over nested dictionaries is standard practice.

own_modules-01.why: Standard idiom taught thoroughly in CS50P.

own_modules-03.why: Requires writing a basic import and function call statement.

assert_statement-01.why: Condition x > 5 is False when x = 3, triggering AssertionError.

assert_statement-02.why: True condition passes silently, prints ok.

assert_statement-03.why: Needs understanding of user input errors vs code bugs.

pytest_testing-01.why: pytest specifically looks for functions starting with test_.

pytest_testing-02.why: Testing even/odd, zero, and negative values covers edge cases best.

pytest_testing-03.why: pytest.raises syntax can be tricky for beginners to recall.

pytest_testing-04.why: Conceptual explanation of robustness and edge cases.

file_io-01.why: Mode 'w' overwrites existing files, a common trap.

file_io-02.why: First 'w' overwrites, then 'a' appends, resulting in both lines.

file_io-03.why: Writing strings with explicit newlines using file write.

with_statement-01.why: Primary reason for context managers is automatic resource cleanup.

with_statement-02.why: Tricky because f is accessible outside the block, and its closed attribute is True.

with_statement-03.why: Resource leaks and file corruption explanation.

csv_files-01.why: DictReader skips header, uses keys to print values.

csv_files-02.why: Classic justification for the csv module regarding commas in quotes.

csv_files-03.why: Requires casting string scores to float/int, summing, and dividing.

operator_overloading-01.why: Students often struggle to follow custom dunder methods like __add__.

operator_overloading-02.why: Writing both __add__ and __eq__ correctly from scratch is challenging.

operator_overloading-03.why: Clear TypeError since + is not defined for Box objects yet.

sets-01.why: Most grasp that sets automatically remove duplicates.

sets-02.why: Requires combining set comprehension/casting with sorted().

sets-03.why: Core lesson emphasizes O(1) membership lookup for sets.

constants_globals-01.why: Demonstrates the necessity of the global keyword.

constants_globals-02.why: Standard convention taught explicitly in CS50P.

constants_globals-03.why: Conceptual question, but reasons are widely covered.

type_hints-01.why: Students learn that Python type hints do not prevent execution.

type_hints-02.why: mypy is explicitly introduced for static type checking.

type_hints-03.why: Standard syntax for returning None in type hints.

argparse_module-01.why: Basic math with parsed integer argument works as expected.

argparse_module-02.why: Main selling point of argparse over sys.argv.

argparse_module-03.why: Syntax for passing a list to parse_args() trips beginners up.

tuples_unpacking-02.why: Tuples are immutable, raising a TypeError.

tuples_unpacking-03.why: Returning min() and max() as a tuple is very common.

args_kwargs-01.why: Direct demonstration of args as tuple and kwargs as dict.

args_kwargs-03.why: Unpacking a list into positional arguments is well practiced.

lambda_functions-01.why: Chaining sorted, lambdas, and indexing requires high cognitive load.

lambda_functions-02.why: Students often get confused by syntax variations of lambdas.

lambda_functions-03.why: Combining sorted(), key parameter, and lambda is tricky for beginners.

map_filter-01.why: Seeing <map object> without list() confuses students, but here list() is used.

map_filter-02.why: Filter is intuitive when paired with a lambda condition.

map_filter-03.why: Iterators exhaust themselves, so the second print prints an empty list.

list_comprehensions-01.why: List comprehensions are widely liked and understood by beginners.

list_comprehensions-02.why: Straightforward application of list comprehensions with string methods.

list_comprehensions-03.why: Option A is the idiomatic Python way taught explicitly.

dict_comprehensions-01.why: Dict comprehension syntax is logical after seeing list comprehensions.

dict_comprehensions-02.why: Swapping keys and values requires iterating over items().

dict_comprehensions-03.why: Dict lookup by key after comprehension is standard practice.

enumerate_function-02.why: Requires starting index at 1, which needs start=1 or i + 1.

enumerate_function-03.why: Enumerate is heavily emphasized as the pythonic way.

generators-01.why: Understanding next() and generator state is moderately tricky.

generators-02.why: Core concept of lazy evaluation in generators is well explained.

generators-03.why: Writing a simple generator with yield is standard.

recursion-01.why: Tracing a summation recursion takes a few steps but is manageable.

recursion-02.why: Missing base case is a classic trap leading to RecursionError.

recursion-03.why: Factorial is the canonical introductory recursive function.

recursion-04.why: Fibonacci is standard, though slightly harder than factorial due to two recursive calls.

recursion-05.why: Recursive palindrome slicing and edge cases are tricky for beginners.

recursion-06.why: Base case and recursive step are drilled into students.

recursion-07.why: Exponential time complexity via overlapping subproblems is a standard conceptual question.

recursion-08.why: Tracing the exact call tree of fib(5) is extremely tedious and error-prone.

logical_operators-03.why: Students often struggle with combining inequalities or inclusive bounds using 'and'.

if_statements-01.why: Beginners often confuse independent if statements with elif and think only one branch runs.

if_statements-02.why: Requires basic comparison and negation, straightforward logic for most.

if_statements-03.why: Missing colon is one of the very first syntax errors students learn.

elif_else-01.why: Standard conditional ladder, though order matters (descending vs ascending).

elif_else-02.why: Tests understanding of mutual exclusivity in elif, a classic trap when order is wrong.

elif_else-03.why: Direct conceptual question about why we use elif instead of multiple ifs.

modulo-01.why: Modulo is a new operator, but 17 % 5 is a standard remainder calculation.

regular_expressions-07.why: Students often struggle with recognizing escape sequences like \s+ and tabs in strings.

raising_exceptions-01.why: Standard conditional check combined with raising an exception is straightforward.

raising_exceptions-02.why: Catches exception and prints message, but beginners might confuse error type with error message.

raising_exceptions-03.why: Emphasizes defensive programming and raising ValueError for invalid initialization.

classes_objects-01.why: Direct dot notation attribute access is one of the first things taught in OOP.

classes_objects-02.why: Concept of self can be abstract for beginners, though heavily emphasized.

classes_objects-03.why: Basic class definition with __init__ and instance methods is standard practice.

classes_objects-04.why: Without __str__, prints memory address; with it, prints custom string. Beginners easily mix this up.

properties_decorators-01.why: Students who understand properties recognize the setter raises a ValueError for invalid input.

properties_decorators-02.why: Infinite recursion is a classic pitfall, but conceptualizing it takes a moment of careful thinking.

properties_decorators-03.why: Writing a class with a property without a setter from scratch requires remembering the underscore naming convention.

class_static_methods-01.why: Straightforward example of a classmethod returning the length of a class list.

class_static_methods-02.why: Covers the primary conceptual use case for @classmethod.

class_static_methods-03.why: Alternative constructors using classmethod with string splitting are tricky for beginners.

inheritance-01.why: Direct application of super().__init__ which is heavily emphasized in lessons.

inheritance-02.why: Clear demonstration of method overriding in subclasses.

inheritance-03.why: Students often forget to call super().__init__(name), leading to AttributeError for missing attributes.

inheritance-04.why: Conceptual question; most grasp the 'is-a' definition well from lecture examples.
